segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Saul approved of his killing. On that day a great persecution arose against the assembly in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Devout men buried Stephen and made loud lamentation over him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Saul was ravaging the assembly; entering house after house, he dragged off both men and women and handed them over to prison.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now those who had been scattered went from place to place proclaiming the good news of the word.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Messiah to them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crowds with one accord paid attention to what Philip was saying, as they listened and saw the signs he was doing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For unclean spirits came out of many who had them, crying out with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed or lame were healed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was great joy in that city.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now a man named Simon had already been in the city practicing magic and astounding the people of Samaria, claiming to be someone great.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All of them, from the least to the greatest, paid attention to him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man is the Power of God that is called Great.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They paid attention to him because for a long time he had astounded them with his magic.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Even Simon himself believed, and after being baptized he stayed close to Philip; and seeing signs and great deeds of power taking place, he was astounded.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who went down and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it had not yet fallen on any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Give me this authority too, so that anyone I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “May your silver go to destruction with you, because you thought you could acquire God’s gift with money!

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So repent of this wickedness of yours, and plead with the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For I see that you are in bitter gall and in the bonds of wrongdoing.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Plead with the Lord for me yourselves, so that nothing of what you have said may come upon me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So then, after they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they made their way back to Jerusalem, proclaiming the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Get up and go toward the south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This is a desert road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he got up and went. And there was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a court official of the Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of her entire treasury. He had come to Jerusalem to worship,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and was returning, seated in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Spirit said to Philip,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Go up and join this chariot.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Do you really understand what you are reading?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How could I, unless someone guides me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the passage of scripture he was reading was this:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: In his humiliation justice was taken away from him. Who will describe his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The eunuch said to Philip in reply,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this: about himself or about someone else?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Philip opened his mouth and, beginning from this scripture, proclaimed to him the good news about Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, water! What prevents me from being baptized?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He ordered the chariot to stop, and both of them went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip, however, was found at Azotus, and passing through he proclaimed the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

notes.note: The Greek word was the ordinary term for a gathering of people, and in the Greek Old Testament it names the assembly of Israel. "Church" is the standard rendering and is not wrong, but to a modern reader it suggests a building or an institution, which the word did not mean at this period. "Assembly" keeps the sense of a gathered community of people.

Here the Greek has the article and uses the word as a title, "the Anointed One", not as part of Jesus' name. Philip is announcing that the awaited anointed king has come. Many recent translations also use "the Messiah" in this verse. In verse 12, where the word stands alongside "Jesus" as a name, "Christ" is kept.

Some manuscripts lack the article, giving "a city of Samaria". With the article, the phrase most naturally means the chief city of the region, though Luke does not name it. Samaria is otherwise the name of the region in this chapter, and which city is meant remains uncertain.

notes.phrase: the Power of God that is called Great
notes.note: "Power" could be used as a title for a divine being or for a manifestation of God himself, so the crowds are acclaiming Simon as something more than a wonder-worker. The exact meaning of the title is debated. Luke plays on the words in verse 13, where the man called the Great Power is himself astounded by great deeds of power.

The Greek uses the plural of the same word, "power", that the crowds applied to Simon in verse 10, with the same adjective, "great". "Miracles" is the usual rendering, but it hides the echo. "Deeds of power" keeps it visible.

The Greek word is the one translated "word" elsewhere in the chapter (verses 4, 14, 25). Peter may mean that Simon has no share in "this word", that is, the message and its work, and not simply in "this matter" of conferring the Spirit. Most translations choose "matter", as here, but the other reading is possible.

notes.phrase: in bitter gall and in the bonds of wrongdoing
notes.traditional: in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity
notes.note: Peter's language echoes Scripture. Deuteronomy 29:18 warns of a person turning from God who becomes a root bearing gall and bitterness, and Isaiah 58:6 speaks of loosing the bonds of injustice. The sense is that Simon is in a poisonous condition and held captive by wrongdoing.

The Greek word means "midday" and, by extension, "the south", where the sun stands at noon. The phrase can therefore also be read "about noon". Most translations take it as a direction, as here, but the time reading is defended by some scholars.

The Greek says only "this is desert" or "deserted". It may be the angel's own words or, as taken here, an aside by the narrator. It may describe the road, or the city of Gaza, whose old site was said to lie abandoned.

Candace (Kandake) was not a personal name but the title of the ruling queens or queen mothers of the kingdom of Meroë. "Ethiopia" in ancient usage meant that Nubian kingdom on the upper Nile, in what is now Sudan, not the modern country of Ethiopia. To readers in the Mediterranean world it stood for the far southern edge of the known world.

Castrated men often served as trusted officials in royal courts, and the word could sometimes be used for a high court officer more generally. If it is meant literally here, as most scholars think, the law of Deuteronomy 23:1 would have barred him from full membership in Israel's assembly, while Isaiah 56:3-5 promises eunuchs a place among God's people.

The quotation is Isaiah 53:7-8 in the old Greek version, which differs somewhat from the Hebrew text. "His generation" may mean his contemporaries, his descendants (he is cut off without any), or his origin. The Greek is as open as the English, and the rendering leaves it so.

notes.phrase: What prevents me from being baptized?
notes.note: Verse 37 is absent from the earliest and best manuscripts and is not printed in the Greek text translated here, so the numbering passes from 36 to 38. In later manuscripts it reads: "Philip said, 'If you believe with all your heart, you may.' He answered, 'I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.'" The words were known by the late second century, but scholars generally regard them as an early addition reflecting baptismal practice.
